summary: TB-500 is a peptide in the repair & anti inflammatory class (thymosin beta-4 fragment; actin sequestration, angiogenesis). Europe PMC indexes 1,257 publications naming it or a listed alias in a title or abstract, including 7 randomized controlled trials and 6 clinical trials of any design, as of 2026-09-14. The strongest evidence tier in that literature is human clinical trials. This page reports what those studies state, sentence by sentence, with each statement tied to its source and labeled by the kind of evidence it is. It does not recommend use, and it does not translate study doses into anything personal.

seo.title: TB-500: Thymosin β4 Trials, Fragment Evidence, Side Effects
seo.description: TB-500: the fragment vs full thymosin beta-4, which human trials exist, the one rat study of injected TB-500, side effects and status.

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2021: administration by intravenous route reported. The study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK) and anti-drug antibody (ADA) of the recombinant human thymosin β4 (NL005) for single and multiple intravenous injections in healthy subjects.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: The study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK) and anti-drug antibody (ADA) of the recombinant human thymosin β4 (NL005) for single and multiple intravenous injections in healthy subjects.
routes_studied.plain: A 2021 first-in-human phase 1 trial in healthy Chinese volunteers gave recombinant human thymosin β4 (NL005, the full natural protein) into a vein, as single and multiple doses.

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=72, 2007: administration by topical route reported. The objective of this double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation study is to evaluate safety, tolerability, and enhancement on healing of thymosin beta-4 (Tbeta-4) administered topically in patients with venous ulcers.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: The objective of this double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation study is to evaluate safety, tolerability, and enhancement on healing of thymosin beta-4 (Tbeta-4) administered topically in patients with venous ulcers.
routes_studied.plain: A 2007 randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-rising trial applied thymosin beta-4 (the full natural protein) to the skin of people with venous leg ulcers.

routes_studied.value: Animal study, mice, 2026: administration by oral route reported. Conversely, oral administration of recombinant human Tβ4 (rhTβ4) significantly improved survival, alleviated body weight loss, reduced epithelial injury, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production in both prophylactic and therapeutic colitis models.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: Conversely, oral administration of recombinant human Tβ4 (rhTβ4) significantly improved survival, alleviated body weight loss, reduced epithelial injury, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production in both prophylactic and therapeutic colitis models.
routes_studied.plain: In mice with colitis (gut inflammation), recombinant human thymosin β4 given by mouth significantly improved survival, reduced weight loss and gut lining injury, and lowered inflammatory signals.

study_doses.value: Animal study, rats, 2026: doses stated in the abstract: 60 µg/kg/day. Thirty-two male Sprague-Dawley rats, each aged 12 weeks and weighing approximately 330 g, underwent standardized Achilles tendon transection and repair and were randomly assigned to four groups, with eight rats in each group: control, BPC-157 (10 µg/kg/day), TB-500 (60 µg/kg/day), and combined BPC-157 + TB-500 (BPC + TB).
study_doses.source_excerpt: Thirty-two male Sprague-Dawley rats, each aged 12 weeks and weighing approximately 330 g, underwent standardized Achilles tendon transection and repair and were randomly assigned to four groups, with eight rats in each group: control, BPC-157 (10 µg/kg/day), TB-500 (60 µg/kg/day), and combined BPC-157 + TB-500 (BPC + TB).
study_doses.plain: In thirty-two male rats after Achilles tendon repair, groups of eight received TB-500 at 60 µg/kg/day, BPC-157 at 10 µg/kg/day, both, or no treatment.

escalation_schedules.plain: A 2007 double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in venous leg ulcers tested rising doses of thymosin beta-4 (the full natural protein) applied to the skin, for safety and healing.

biomarkers_monitored.value: Human study, humans, n=43, 2025: Although thymosin beta 4 has shown cardioprotective effects in preclinical MI models, its impact on chronic cardiac functional recovery post ischemia/reperfusion (I/R), especially in STEMI, warrants further investigation.

biomarkers_monitored.value: In vitro study, human donor cells (adipose-derived stem cells), 2024: In previous studies, it was confirmed that thymosin beta 4 (Tβ4) could enhance fat survival in vivo, although the precise mechanism remains unclear.

study_durations.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2021: durations stated: 10 days; 28 days. A total of 30 healthy subjects were randomly enrolled in the multiple-dose trial, and 3 cohorts (0.5, 2.0 and 5.0 μg/kg) were administered once human thymosin β4 daily for 10 days and observed for 28 days.

study_durations.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=5, 2016: durations stated: 6 months. After 6 months of follow-up, the average 6-min walking distance was increased by 38.2 m (from 263 ± 42 m to 302 ± 34 m) in the control group and 75.7 m (from 264 ± 42 m to 340 ± 44 m) in the experimental group; the average difference of the 6-min walking distance was 37.5 m (95% confidence interval [CI], 28.7-56.3 m; P Discussion Our pilot study suggested that Tβ4-optimized EPC transplantation appeared to be feasible and safe, and might have beneficial effects on exercise capacity and left ventricular function in patients with STEMI.

study_durations.value: Human study, humans, n=43, 2025: durations stated: 7 day; 28 days; 1 day. Methods and results In C57BL/6J mice, 7-day rhTB4 treatment prevented cardiac dysfunction and fibrosis 28 days post-I/R surgery and significantly reduced plasma NT-proBNP levels at both 1 day and 28 days post-I/R.

regulatory_status.value: Not approved anywhere: neither the fragment nor the full protein has a marketing authorisation. Thymosin beta-4 products reached phase 2 and 3 trials in eye and wound conditions without approval. TB-500 is named on the WADA Prohibited List under S2 (peptide hormones, growth factors, related substances and mimetics), prohibited at all times. TB-500 was among the peptides scheduled for FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee in July 2026; secondary reports say the committee recommended adding it to the compounding list; that is unverified here until FDA's own record is in the ledger, and it does not make TB-500 prescribable yet.

mechanism.value: Thymosin beta-4 is a 43-amino-acid protein present in almost every human cell, where it binds actin and regulates how cells build their skeleton and move. What is sold as TB-500 is usually a short synthetic fragment, seven amino acids from the protein's actin-binding region (positions 17 to 23), although some vendors sell the full protein under the same name. This page's ledger indexes both under the compound's aliases, and the distinction matters for every sentence about evidence.

The proposed healing mechanism follows from actin biology: by binding actin, thymosin beta-4 promotes the migration of cells into a wound, encourages new blood-vessel formation, reduces inflammation and scarring, and in heart-attack models in animals protects cardiac muscle. These effects are documented for the full protein in animals and cells; whether the seven-amino-acid fragment reproduces them when injected has been tested in very few studies.

The human evidence belongs to the full protein, developed by RegeneRx under the names RGN-259 (eye drops), RGN-137 (topical gel) and RGN-352 (intravenous). Those trials span dry eye and neurotrophic keratopathy, chronic wounds and epidermolysis bullosa, and a phase 1 intravenous safety study in healthy volunteers. No trial has tested injected TB-500 fragment for any indication; the one indexed study of injected TB-500 for healing is the 2026 rat tendon study that also tested BPC-157.

reported_use.value: TB-500 circulates for injury recovery, tendon and ligament healing, hair and, more speculatively, heart health, injected subcutaneously or intramuscularly on a weekly schedule, and most often paired with BPC-157 as the Wolverine stack. Reported effects are faster recovery and reduced pain; reported side effects are injection-site reactions, transient fatigue, headache and light-headedness. None of this comes from a human study of the fragment. Figures for this compound circulate on forums and vendor pages. None has been tested in a human study, so none is reproduced here; the table above holds every dose a study actually administered.

faq.question: What is TB-500?
faq.answer: Usually a seven-amino-acid fragment of thymosin beta-4, a protein present in nearly every cell that regulates actin and cell movement. Some products sold as TB-500 are the full 43-amino-acid protein.

faq.question: Is TB-500 the same as thymosin beta-4?
faq.answer: Not usually. TB-500 is typically the actin-binding fragment; thymosin beta-4 is the full protein, which is what the human trials tested.

faq.question: Has TB-500 been tested in humans?
faq.answer: The fragment has not. The full protein has phase 1 to 3 trials as eye drops, topical gel and intravenous infusion.

faq.question: What does TB-500 do?
faq.answer: In animals and cells the full protein promotes cell migration into wounds, new blood vessels, and reduced scarring, and protects heart muscle in injury models. The fragment's injected effects rest on one rat tendon study.

faq.question: Is there a TB-500 dose?
faq.answer: No human dose has been studied for the fragment. Trial doses of the full protein are listed above by route; figures that circulate for injection are untested and not reproduced here.

faq.question: What are the side effects of TB-500?
faq.answer: The intravenous phase 1 study of the full protein found no dose-limiting toxicity over two weeks. Community reports of the fragment describe injection-site reactions, fatigue and headache. Long-term effects are unknown.

faq.question: Is TB-500 FDA approved?
faq.answer: No, and neither is thymosin beta-4. TB-500 was considered by FDA's compounding advisory committee in July 2026; secondary reports say the committee recommended adding it to the compounding list. FDA's own record is not yet in this ledger, and a recommendation does not make it prescribable.

faq.question: Is TB-500 banned in sport?
faq.answer: Yes. Named on the WADA Prohibited List under S2, prohibited at all times.

faq.question: Can BPC-157 and TB-500 be used together?
faq.answer: Communities do, as the Wolverine stack. One 2026 rat tendon study tested the pair; no human study has.

faq.question: Does TB-500 help hair growth?
faq.answer: Thymosin beta-4 promotes hair follicle cell migration in mice. No human study of TB-500 or the protein for hair exists.

faq.question: Is TB-500 good for the heart?
faq.answer: The full protein protects heart muscle in animal injury models and one small uncontrolled human study reported improved walking distance. No controlled human evidence.

faq.question: What is TB-500's half-life?
faq.answer: The full protein is cleared from plasma within hours after infusion. The fragment's half-life in people has not been measured.

faq.question: How should TB-500 be stored?
faq.answer: Powder refrigerated or frozen away from light; reconstituted solution refrigerated and used within about four weeks.

faq.question: TB-500 vs BPC-157: which is better?
faq.answer: Neither has controlled human evidence for healing; they act by different proposed mechanisms; one rat study tested both without ranking them.

faq.question: How many TB-500 studies exist?
faq.answer: 1,257 indexed publications for thymosin beta-4 and its aliases, mostly basic cell biology; 25 primary studies are tabulated here, 14 of them in humans and all of those on the full protein.

faq.question: Who developed thymosin beta-4 as a drug?
faq.answer: RegeneRx, as RGN-259 eye drops, RGN-137 gel and RGN-352 intravenous, through phase 2 and 3 trials without approval.

guide.heading: TB-500 in two minutes
guide.html:
What it is. Usually a seven-amino-acid fragment of thymosin beta-4, a protein in nearly every cell that regulates actin and cell movement.{{cite:pmid-16099219}} Some products sold as TB-500 are the full 43-amino-acid protein.

What the research actually shows. 1,257 indexed publications because the protein is a basic cell-biology molecule. Human trials exist for the full protein: eye drops for dry eye and corneal disease, a topical gel for chronic wounds, and an intravenous safety study in 40 volunteers.{{cite:pmid-25826322}}{{cite:pmid-17495250}}{{cite:pmid-20536470}}{{cite:pmid-20536472}} For the injected fragment: one rat tendon study, shared with BPC-157.{{cite:pmid-42542926}} No human trial.

Status. Not approved anywhere; WADA S2, prohibited at all times; under FDA compounding review in 2026.

Where the evidence is thinnest. Whether injecting the fragment does anything the full protein does, and everything about it in people.

guide.heading: Who TB-500 is discussed for, and the cautions that recur
guide.html:
The interest. Tendon, ligament and muscle injuries, and recovery generally; the audience overlaps almost entirely with BPC-157's.

  • Cancer. Thymosin beta-4 promotes cell migration and blood-vessel growth and is elevated in several tumours;{{cite:pmid-36321670}}{{cite:pmid-34081824}} whether supplementing it matters in a person with a tumour is untested and is the caution every review lists first.
  • Athletes. Named on the WADA list, prohibited at all times, detectable.
  • Which molecule is in the vial. Fragment or full protein, at unknown purity; the two are not interchangeable and a certificate of analysis is the only check.
  • Pregnancy, children. No data.

guide.heading: What is measured over time, and what is not
guide.html: The full protein is cleared from plasma within hours after infusion.{{cite:pmid-20536472}} Eye and wound trials measured change over weeks.{{cite:pmid-25826322}}{{cite:pmid-17495250}} Nothing has been measured after injecting the fragment in a person; the recovery timelines that circulate are self-report over periods in which injuries heal anyway.

guide.heading: Storage and handling
guide.html: Powder refrigerated or frozen away from light; reconstituted solution refrigerated and used within about four weeks. Discard cloudy or discoloured solution. The full protein and the fragment have different molecular weights, so the same labelled mass is a different number of molecules.

guide.heading: Common mistakes in how TB-500 is discussed
guide.html:
• Quoting thymosin beta-4 trials as TB-500 evidence. Eye drops and wound gels of the full protein say nothing about an injected fragment.
  • Counting 1,257 publications as support. Most are cell biology of a ubiquitous protein.
  • Reading the 2010 phase 1 study as safety data for what is sold. It was the full protein, intravenous, in healthy people, for two weeks.{{cite:pmid-20536472}}
  • Assuming the Wolverine stack was studied in people. One rat study.{{cite:pmid-42542926}}
